<thought>The 13C NMR spectrum shows the following chemical shifts: 168.30, 130.70, 130.27, 128.35, 126.66, 124.85, 123.57, 58.70, 36.40, 36.40, 26.40. All values are distinct except 36.40, which appears twice, indicating two equivalent carbons. Therefore, the number of unique carbon environments is the count of distinct shifts, which is 10.</thought>
<final_answer>10</final_answer>
